module_title: Intermediate Timeline - History of Poverty Estimation Committees
introduction: Poverty line estimation in India has evolved from counting calories to measuring multidimensional expenditure. This level covers the chronological sequence of the four major poverty committees and their exact benchmarks, which are guaranteed questions in match-the-following formats.

core_concepts.title: Y.K. Alagh Committee (1979)
core_concepts.description:
- **Core Metric:** Introduced the concept of the poverty line based on **nutritional requirements (Calories)**.
- **Benchmarks:** Established a daily minimum requirement of **2400 calories for Rural areas** and **2100 calories for Urban areas**.

core_concepts.title: Lakdawala Committee (1993)
core_concepts.description:
- **Core Metric:** Retained the calorie framework but introduced **State-Specific Poverty Lines**.
- **Inflation Indexing:** Used CPI-IL (Industrial Workers) for urban areas and CPI-AL (Agricultural Labourers) for rural areas to update poverty lines.

core_concepts.title: Suresh Tendulkar Committee (2009)
core_concepts.description:
- **Core Metric:** Shifted away from calorie intake to **Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE)**. Included expenditure on health and education for the first time.
- **Benchmarks (2011-12 data):** Set the poverty line at **₹27 per day (Rural)** and **₹33 per day (Urban)**.
- **Result:** Estimated India's poverty rate at **21.9%**.

core_concepts.title: C. Rangarajan Committee (2014)
core_concepts.description:
- **Core Metric:** Reverted partially to normative needs (adequate nourishment, clothing, rent, conveyance).
- **Benchmarks (2011-12 data):** Raised the poverty line to **₹32 per day (Rural)** and **₹47 per day (Urban)**.
- **Result:** Estimated India's poverty rate at **29.5%**. (Note: The government did not officially adopt Rangarajan's higher poverty estimates).

important_entities.name: Tendulkar's 21.9%
important_entities.significance: The poverty figure of 21.9% (based on Tendulkar methodology for 2011-12) is the last official, widely cited poverty percentage before India shifted to the Multidimensional Poverty Index.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often get confused: Rural people need *more* calories (2400 vs 2100) due to heavy physical labor, but the monetary poverty line is *lower* for rural areas (₹27 vs ₹33) because the cost of living and food is cheaper in villages compared to cities.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use the acronym ALTR to remember the exact chronological order of the poverty estimation committees. (Think of it as 'Altering' poverty lines).

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC Prelims and Banking exams frequently test the exact parameters of the Tendulkar Committee. Remember that Tendulkar was the first to explicitly include private expenditure on 'Health and Education' in the poverty basket.
